definitions.explanation: Used with の to mark something as 'real', 'actual', or 'by blood'. Appears in a small set of common patterns including biological-family terms and rhetorical phrases that contrast the actual with the apparent.

examples.japanese: {実|じつ}の{母親|ははおや}に{会|あ}った。
{実|じつ}を{言|い}うと、まだ{決|き}めていない。
examples.english: To tell the truth, I haven't decided yet.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{義理|ぎり}の{姉|あね}で、{実|じつ}の{姉|あね}ではない。
examples.english: She's my sister-in-law, not my biological sister.

notes:
Sino-Japanese reading of {実} meaning 'real' or 'actual'. Functions as a noun mainly in the fixed pattern {実|じつ}の〜 (biological/real ~) and a few set phrases. The same kanji is also read み (fruit; substance) as a separate everyday word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {実|じつ}の{母|はは} / {父|ちち} / {兄|あに} / {姉|あね}: biological mother/father/brother/sister
- {実|じつ}の{親|おや}: biological parent
- {実|じつ}を{言|い}うと / {実|じつ}を{言|い}えば: to tell the truth
- {実|じつ}のところ: actually; in fact
- {実|じつ}は: actually (sentence-initial)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {本当|ほんとう}: real; true — the everyday equivalent
- {現実|げんじつ}: reality — abstract; the real world as opposed to imagination
- {本物|ほんもの}: the real thing — refers to objects, contrasted with fakes
